key_insight: In RL with verifiable rewards, larger EMA momentum can help—if it is increased enough to stay in a stable, non-overshooting regime.
engineering_relevance: For LLM post-training and RLVR, tuning momentum upward can yield better sample efficiency and validation accuracy than using conventional small momentum values.
method: Analyze a bandit model of RLVR with bias-corrected EMA momentum.
Prove that, under exact gradients, larger EMA coefficients accelerate optimization before overshoot.
Show that with sampled gradients, keeping η/(1−β) in the safe regime preserves a gain that beats sampling noise as η shrinks.
evidence_signal: Bandit simulations and RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen2.5-32B (with SGD/EMA and AdamW) validate the theory, including nearly 2 percentage points higher mean validation accuracy from increasing β1.
watch_item: Momentum must be increased carefully; if the effective step size becomes too large, overshoot can negate the benefit.
paper_title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
